author: WP15
summary: Avatar chapter: the faithfully inert XNA avatar API, the SkinnedModelEXT contract and palette maths, lighting, appearance and wardrobe, the content format and its traps, the open garment interpenetration and the renderer evidence. Almost entirely current (one static-vs-instance event correction and a retired-family remark). libcna.com had only passing mentions (Tutorial 123, Tutorial 57, the XNA compatibility page), so the substance now lives on a new Avatars deep dive.

sections.heading: Avatar: Faithful Absence and CNAEXT Rendering

concepts.section: Avatar: Faithful Absence and CNAEXT Rendering
concepts.text: CNA has two independent avatar systems: the XNA-compatible classes reproduce the observable behaviour of a reference assembly whose content service is gone and are inert, while the SkinnedModelEXT extension loads and renders content; calling the extension does not change the base API's state or semantics.
tokens: Calling the extension never changes what the XNA members report

concepts.section: Avatar: Faithful Absence and CNAEXT Rendering
concepts.text: Comparison: the base API has a fixed 71-transform contract and validates then draws nothing; the extension has a content-defined skeleton (19 bones in the bundled assets), draws through GraphicsDevice/SkinnedEffect, needs explicit opt-in and has content, renderer and pixel tests.
tokens: Content-defined; the bundled male and female bodies have 19 bones

concepts.section: Avatar: Faithful Absence and CNAEXT Rendering
concepts.text: 'Faithful' is scoped to translated behaviour and tests; it does not mean the C++ port is binary-identical to the managed assembly or that Xbox avatar services exist.
AvatarRenderer ignores both constructor arguments.
Reading AvatarRenderer::State sets and returns AvatarRendererState::Unavailable on every read; no path reaches Ready or Loading.
The IAvatarAnimation Draw overload rejects null, reads the transforms and expression and delegates; the transform-array overload requires exactly 71 entries and then does nothing.
tokens: Both Draw overloads validate and stop.

concepts.text: AvatarRenderer::BindPose throws InvalidOperationException unless the unreachable Ready state is present.
AvatarDescription requires exactly 1,021 bytes and treats a correctly sized value as valid when byte zero is non-zero; the other bytes are opaque.
The description getter copies the bytes, Height and BodyType default lazily (0.0 and Female), and the Changed event is never raised; at the snapshot Changed is a per-instance event, not a static one.
Both CreateRandom overloads return the same all-zero invalid description; the body-type overload validates its enum but does not use it.
tokens: the same all-zero, therefore invalid, description

concepts.text: BeginGetFromGamer/EndGetFromGamer complete synchronously and return the invalid description; the caller owns and must delete the heap-allocated IAsyncResult.
tokens: BeginGetFromGamer throws for a null or disposed gamer

concepts.text: AvatarAnimation supplies 71 zero transforms, zero duration and a default expression for all 31 presets; the preset survives only as the CNAEXT clip name returned by GetRealClipNameEXT.

These results are expected because the service-supplied mesh, texture, animation and description data are unavailable; FNA has no avatar classes, so CNA translated the source from the XNA 4.0 reference assembly.
tokens: FNA has no avatar classes at all

concepts.text: SkinnedModelEXT is move-only because it owns GPU resources.

SkinnedModelEXT holds parent indices, local bind poses and global inverse bind poses, named clips of per-bone translation/scale/rotation tracks, and named parts with vertex, index and texture resources (no separate material object).
tokens: there is no per-part material object beyond the texture

concepts.text: The extension skeleton is unrelated to AvatarRenderer's 71-entry array; the bundled male and female assets use 19 bones and other content may use up to SkinnedEffect's 72-bone limit.

EnableRealRenderingEXT(device, model) creates the extension's SkinnedEffect; DrawRealEXT(clip, position, loop) samples and draws or throws InvalidOperationException without opt-in; it neither makes State ready nor gives the base Draw a renderer.
Conventional content roots are avatar/male/avatar and avatar/female/avatar, produced by AvatarBodyTypeToContentNameEXT.

ComputeBoneTransformsEXT initialises locals from the bind pose, samples matching tracks (lerp translation/scale, Quaternion::Slerp rotation), composes children with already computed parents in stored topological order and multiplies each global transform by its inverse bind pose to form the SkinnedEffect palette.
Looped time uses tick modulo instead of repeated subtraction, including for negative time.
tokens: Looped time uses one tick modulo, including negative time

concepts.text: Each non-root parent must precede its child, which also rejects cycles.
Skeleton arrays must match BoneCount before indexing.
Empty or out-of-range animation tracks are skipped without touching memory.
The time regression test samples a position 1,000,000,000.5 clip durations from the origin with a 100 ms bound, detecting the former duration-by-duration loop.

The extension uses one directional light plus ambient: it disables the other two stock directional lights and zeroes specular and emissive before applying the caller's values; default ambient and key light keep an avatar visible without configuration.

AvatarAppearanceEXT is a CNA tint model, not a reconstruction of the proprietary format: case-sensitive part-name substrings select Hair, Shirt, Pants or Shoes, unmatched names receive the skin tint, and it changes colours only.

AttachPartEXT requires a matching bone count; re-attaching a same-named part first calls RemovePartEXT, which releases the old owned buffers, mesh part and texture, closing both the overlapping-part behaviour and its GPU-resource leak.
Historical: an early avatar draw path used EnableDefaultLighting, which leaked the generic fill and back lights and could overwrite the ambient term.
concepts.note: Fixed at TARGET: DrawRealEXT configures one key light, disables lights 1 and 2 and sets ambient last with no EnableDefaultLighting call. Told as history on the avatars page (#lighting-history).

concepts.text: Historical: a GL stock-shader defect multiplied the emissive (ambient-folded) colour by diffuse twice, turning ambient into ambient x diffuse^2 for skinned, vertex-lit and environment-mapped variants; the avatar's near-black fraction fell from 4.1-6.0 % to 0 % after alignment with FNA.
concepts.note: Fixed at TARGET with a discriminating test (EasyGL_EmissiveAmbientComposition, Vulkan_EmissiveAmbientComposition); told as a historical lesson on the avatars page (#lighting-history).

concepts.text: Extension assets load from a .skinnedmodel.json manifest with .skeleton.bin and .clip.bin sidecars.
Manifest-relative paths must resolve from the manifest's directory, not the content root.
tokens: Resolve sidecars from the manifest's own directory.

concepts.text: Chained reader.Read<float>() constructor arguments relied on unspecified argument evaluation order; components are now read into named locals.
Hierarchy reordering must remap inverse bind matrices and per-vertex joint indices as well as parent indices.
The corresponding glTF joint-space rules belong to glTF skinning, where skinned glTF/.cnj content loads as a Model with SkinningData rather than SkinnedModelEXT.

The procedural avatar still shows shirt and skin fragments around the raised shoulder and chest in Wave; the same 64 of 228 shirt vertices cross the body in both neutral and Wave poses, locating the defect in rest-pose geometry, not clip sampling.
concepts.note: Reported from CNA's own record at TARGET; not re-measured.

concepts.text: The visible intersections are the collar and cuffs: the shirt's Spine1 shell (radius about 0.176) overlaps the head sphere (radius 0.15), measured collar penetration 0.131 m, while the waist overlap is mutually hidden.
concepts.note: Radii derivable from the generators; the z-extents and overlap arithmetic are the record's, not re-derived.

concepts.text: Four remedies failed: narrowing the garment blend radius, trimming capsule caps (pants crossings 21 to 39), flat cylinders plus joint spheres (more speckle, new groin crossings, lower brightness) and 32 instead of 12 segments (smoother, same fragments, 4.2x vertex data).

Open choices: size collar and cuff shells against the body radii along their span, accept convex per-bone shells, or accept the tessellation cost; the extension is renderer-functional but not visually defect-free.
tokens: renderer-functional with a known cosmetic limitation

concepts.text: EasyGL and Vulkan register the avatar integration programs with pixel readback.
Their synthetic one-bone quads isolate palette/effect/draw wiring and do not validate the asset converter.
Demo programs add full humanoid content, clip changes, appearance, attachment, wardrobe replacement, API-boundary comparison and two-process network synchronisation.

Other GPU families have no registered avatar integration result at the snapshot (the claim's specific harness remark concerned a renderer family that has since been retired); only EasyGL and Vulkan register the programs.
concepts.note: The harness-stops-early detail referred to a retired renderer family; not reproduced. Post-Phase-3 adversarial audit correction: the ledger correction was wrong: OPENGL4 registers the avatar programs through the EasyGL parity corpus (audit finding C10 ch52-F1; CNA-VGAP-040 says so).

target.evidence: grep of renderer example CMake files for avatar_*_integration_test.cpp (easygl, vulkan only)

concepts.text: SDL_RENDERER rejects the 3D resources the extension needs.
tokens: throw on the first 3D resource the extension creates

concepts.text: No conclusion for any other renderer should be inferred from EasyGL or Vulkan avatar pixels.
tokens: nothing about avatar rendering on them should be inferred

issues.text: Dispose(bool) visibility: AvatarRenderer's Dispose(bool) is protected at TARGET, but Accelerometer, Gyroscope, Compass and Motion still declare Dispose(bool) public while SensorBase declares it protected, so an external Dispose(false) reaches the base path that marks the sensor disposed without cleanup.
issues.evidence: modules/gamer-services/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/GamerServices/AvatarRenderer.hpp (protected Dispose(bool)); modules/devices/include/Microsoft/Devices/Sensors/Accelerometer.hpp, Gyroscope.hpp, Compass.hpp, Motion.hpp (public Dispose(bool)); SensorBase.hpp (protected virtual Dispose(bool)); modules/devices/src/Sensors/Accelerometer.cpp (!disposing branch)

issues.text: The bundled procedural avatar's garment shells interpenetrate the body (collar and cuffs visible; shirt 64/228 vertices crossing), per CNA's own record; four remedies were measured and reverted.

Avatar rendering evidence is three pixel programs on EasyGL and Vulkan using a synthetic one-bone quad; no renderer test validates the bundled 19-bone content, and no other renderer registers the programs.
SkinnedModelEXT::AttachPartEXT only checks BoneCount equality; a different skeleton with the same bone count is not detected.
docs/avatar-real-rendering-ext.md's renderer table still says Vulkan was not yet smoke-tested although the Vulkan examples CMake registers the three avatar programs (documentation staleness in CNA).
The XNA avatar API is inert (State Unavailable, Draw no-op, zero descriptions/animations) by fidelity to the reference assembly without its service; not a defect.
